routes.name: The Founders' Walk
routes.description: Follow the Stanford family's story, from Leland Jr.'s tomb and the garden of their unbuilt mansion to the church Jane built for Leland.

routes.name: Big Game Day
routes.description: Big Game week: the Bearial at The Claw, Gaieties at Mem Aud, then on to the stadium where Cal won the first game in 1921.

routes.name: The 1906 Earthquake Walk
routes.description: April 18, 1906, 5:12 AM. See what fell and what stood: the tomb that came through untouched, the wrecked museum, the lost arch and spire, and the library destroyed before it opened.

routes.name: The Farm & the Presidents
routes.description: Why Stanford is "the Farm": from Leland Stanford's horse barn and reservoir to the hilltop homes of a Stanford president and a U.S. president.

routes.name: One Piece of Land
routes.description: One piece of land, told forward in time: the horse farm, the reservoir dug for it, the garden of a mansion never built, the family's grave, and the Quad where the garden's palms ended up.
bridge: Everything on this walk was once one property: Leland Stanford's Palo Alto Stock Farm, which at its height boarded 600 horses.
The farm needed water. In 1878 this lake was built as its stock pond and reservoir.
Near the farm, the Stanfords planned a country mansion, and in the early 1880s they had this garden laid out beside its site.
The mansion was never built. In 1884 their only son died at 15, and the family's fortune turned toward a memorial in his name.
A few steps from the family tomb stands a second memorial, this one to Jane Stanford's youngest brother.
The memorial they chose was a university. Look at the palms in the Quad's circles: thirty of them were dug up from the cactus garden you just visited.
routes.outro: That's one piece of land: a horse farm, the reservoir dug for it, the garden of a mansion never built, the family's grave, and the university that grew from them.

prologue.text: Before the farm. About 3.4 km north, by the Caltrain tracks at Alma Street and Palo Alto Avenue, stands El Palo Alto, the tall tree. In 1769 Gaspar de Portolá's expedition, 63 men with 200 horses and mules, camped near the tall tree while looking for Monterey Bay. Finding the bay too large to go around, they turned back to San Diego. In 1774 Father Palóu planted a cross at the site. Today it is California Historical Landmark No. 2.

side.text: Side quest: Hanna House, Frank Lloyd Wright's honeycomb house, about 2 km from the Quad. It is exterior only: view it from the road and don't enter the grounds.
